# Seungah Seo

I am a Ph.D. student in social welfare.

At the center of my work is human action — action that carries a plurality of meanings, relations, and institutional conditions that cannot be reduced to any single factor. I am interested in what gets lost when “the social” is explained through a single cause or through individuals alone. I look for these irreducible layers across emotion, social frailty, and institutional practice.

## Research Interests

- Emotion and relationship in later life
- Frailty and social frailty
- Institutions and practice in social policy

## Current Work

- **Social frailty** — early-stage work toward a critical review of how the “social” in social frailty is conceptualized, and what individual-level measures leave out
- **Emotion in later-life narratives** — a text analysis of how older adults express emotion and relationship in oral life histories
- **Institutional decoupling in social policy** — an analysis of the gap between formal policy and actual practice, reconceptualizing decoupling as a matter of action rather than only as formal conformity or strategic evasion
- **Youth suicide prevention** — qualitative research on service access, care discontinuities, and institutional gaps among young adults at high risk of suicide; presented at APHA 2026
